rationale: Economically coherent, correctly signed, and a genuine single-share functional form rather than a rank blend, but it is largely the mechanical union of two already-evaluated archive signals (RolloverBurdenPerCashFlow and ExternalFundingShare) and mixes a stock (dlc) with flows (sstk, dltis) in the same numerator, so incremental information beyond the parents is questionable.

This is a textbook interest-coverage ratio — a long-published distress/leverage proxy — and it is also nearly the same construct already used as the conditioning leg of the archive's CoverageConditionedBorrowing (xint over MAX(oibdp, dp)), so it adds little beyond a known credit-risk measure with a substituted denominator.

Replacing the debt level with maturity composition is a legitimately different financing attribute and the two legs of the MIN point the same economic way so the sign is internally consistent, but it remains structurally close to the already-failed RolloverAgainstCashFlowRisk and debt-maturity/stock-return effects are themselves partly documented, so the novelty is incremental rather than fundamental.

The weakest-link conjunction on the long side is a real portfolio-construction difference rather than a sign flip of CashBurningIssuer, and the expected sign matches the expression, but the two legs are essentially cash-based operating profitability and low external financing — two separately published anomalies — so a positive result would be hard to attribute to a novel interaction.

Cumulating both cash generation and gross external raising over five years is a substantively different, low-turnover stock-like characteristic that directly addresses the diagnosed instability of the single-year positive-sign signals, though it overlaps in spirit with multi-year composite-issuance measures and the current-assets denominator against five-year sums should be interpreted with care.

This is an industry-standardized restatement of the already-evaluated NearTermClaimsCoverageGap — a useful robustness diagnostic but precisely the kind of cosmetic transformation of an existing signal that the objective asks to avoid as a new proposal.
